title: Whispering Wisely: Smart Subset Selection for ASR Fine-Tuning
abstract: arXiv:2610.32997v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models such as OpenAIs Whisper have substantially improved speech recognition quality but remain expensive to fine-tune, especially when large amounts of transcribed audio are available. This makes it challenging for many practitioners to adapt these models to new languages or domains. In this work, we introduce an embedding-based subset selection approach for selecting smaller training sets for ASR fine-tuning.

abstract: arXiv:2610.33001v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Academic revision presents a governance problem when legitimate writing objectives conflict. Writing-process and social-science research show that revision is recursive and that wording carries epistemic and disciplinary commitments. abstract: arXiv:2610.33004v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is essential for digitizing historical archives, yet standard evaluation metrics such as Character Error Rate (CER) do not necessarily reflect whether meaningful information, such as names, dates, and identifiers, is preserved. abstract: arXiv:2610.33005v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Energy-based models have shown promising properties for domain-specific tasks but remain challenging in modeling general-purpose scenarios. title: Linear-Time Context Compression with State-Space Encoding
abstract: arXiv:2610.33006v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) impose substantial computation and memory costs as context sizes increase, motivating methods that compress a context into a shorter representation before inference. abstract: arXiv:2610.33007v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Natural-language service intents in integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial (TN/NTN) 6G networks can be incomplete, ambiguous, or inconsistent, making unconstrained LLM generation challenging for reliable network-facing orchestration. title: TraceQuery: learning what to recompute from full-denoising trajectory in diffusion language models
abstract: arXiv:2610.33008v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible generation through iterative masked denoising, but incur substantial inference cost because token representations are repeatedly recomputed across denoising steps. Existing cache-based methods reduce this cost by reusing intermediate results across denoising steps and recomputing only a subset of positions at each step, chosen either on a fixed schedule or by heuristic signals of change. title: Recursive Semantic Divergence for LLM Agent Consistency
abstract: arXiv:2610.33012v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents with tool use exhibit inconsistent behavior across independent runs from identical states, calling different tools, producing contradictory outputs, or pursuing divergent strategies. This variability compounds over time and undermines deployment reliability. Existing evaluation metrics primarily measure task correctness via completion-based scores and do not capture consistency in agent behavior across executions.

title: The Social World Model Evaluation Gap
abstract: arXiv:2610.33014v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A negotiation assistant can reach a good deal without accurately predicting the other person's response. We ask whether evaluations of social world models test that prediction directly. abstract: arXiv:2610.33015v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-term memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to maintain personalized and temporally coherent interactions, but repeated LLM inference for memory admission, extraction, and organization introduces substantial cost and latency. abstract: arXiv:2610.33016v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Llama-3, Qwen3 and many other open LLMs pre-tokenize text with a regular expression whose word class admits only Unicode letters. abstract: arXiv:2610.33017v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multilingual tokenizers trained on English-dominated corpora often over-segment Indic languages, resulting in longer token sequences and increased tokenization disparity across scripts. abstract: arXiv:2610.33018v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Scholarly Knowledge Graphs (SKGs) support literature search, scientific discovery, and agent-assisted research. abstract: arXiv:2610.33020v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: If your brain were connected directly to someone else's, would you still know which thoughts were yours? abstract: arXiv:2610.33027v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Next-token prediction (NTP) rewards only the token that occurs next, penalizing every alternative. title: Lessons from Luck: Do LLM-Written Lessons Carry Chance into an Agent's Next Decision?
abstract: arXiv:2610.33029v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Self-improving agents write lessons from the outcomes of their runs; when outcomes are noisy, a lesson can carry chance into later decisions. abstract: arXiv:2610.33044v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Embodied vision-language models must answer questions from partial, evolving observations.
